title: Deep Current
desc: Ocean trenches, mass extinctions & the species we're only just discovering

questions.q: Scientists estimate we've only identified what percentage of all species on Earth?
questions.a: About 10-15% — roughly 8.7 million species are estimated to exist, and we've catalogued around 1.2 million

questions.q: What is a 'mass extinction event' and how many have there been?
questions.a: A period where at least 75% of species die off globally. There have been five major ones — some scientists argue we're in the sixth right now

questions.q: The giant squid wasn't filmed alive in its natural habitat until which year?
questions.a: 2012 — despite centuries of sailor stories, the first footage was captured by a Japanese-led team in the Pacific

questions.q: What is 'bioluminescence' used for by deep-sea creatures?
questions.a: Hunting (luring prey), defence (blinding predators or triggering a 'burglar alarm'), camouflage (counter-illumination to hide their silhouette from below), and communication

questions.q: Why do trees in a forest often grow to roughly the same height?
questions.a: Competition for light — growing taller than your neighbours costs energy. An equilibrium forms where going higher yields diminishing returns ('the crown shyness' effect also keeps canopies from touching)

questions.q: The Permian-Triassic extinction killed 96% of marine species. What's its nickname?
questions.a: The Great Dying — roughly 252 million years ago, likely triggered by volcanic eruptions in Siberia

questions.q: What is CRISPR's natural role in bacteria — before scientists co-opted it for gene editing?
questions.a: An immune system — bacteria store snippets of virus DNA so they can recognise and destroy that virus if it attacks again

questions.q: Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the ocean floor but support what percentage of marine species?
questions.a: About 25% — they're the most biodiverse marine ecosystems on Earth

questions.q: What is an 'extremophile' and where's the most extreme place we've found life on Earth?
questions.a: An organism thriving in extreme conditions. Candidates: 4km deep in gold mines (Desulforudis), superheated hydrothermal vents (121°C), or the Atacama Desert's hyperarid core

questions.q: Why do migratory birds fly in a V formation?
questions.a: Aerodynamic drafting — each bird flies in the upwash from the wingtip vortex of the bird ahead, reducing energy expenditure by up to 70%. They rotate the lead position to share the effort
